description: Create and activate a subscription calendar from structured events. Extract the schedule yourself first. Free within feed allowances. No automatic monitoring is enrolled. Reuse request_id on retries. publication.status reports calendar-file preparation, not subscription access. Check distribution_ready for access at the reported revision; use get_feed_status for current availability. These tools manage Smart Calendars feeds only; they cannot access mailboxes or start source monitoring, scheduled PDF checks or document refreshes. For requests solely for those unsupported actions, explain the limitation without reading feeds or substituting an edit. For unsupported mailbox requests, offer to work with schedule content the user chooses to provide instead. General ICS explanations need no account access. When sharing a feed or filtered_subscription with distribution_ready=true, offer "Open in calendar app" using that object’s HTTPS subscription_open_url (it redirects to webcal), and "Calendar options" using its subscription_options_url for Apple/default, Google, Outlook and copy-link choices. Retain subscription_url as a copyable HTTPS fallback. Prefer these HTTPS handoff links over putting subscription_webcal_url directly in chat, because some clients do not preserve clickable webcal links. If a handoff URL is absent, use the HTTPS subscription_url and dashboard subscription controls instead. Offer "View or edit" using the feed’s manage_url. For a filtered selection use the nested filtered_subscription links, not the unfiltered feed links. Use the returned URLs exactly; never invent or rewrite their host, path or token. Opening a link does not confirm a subscription; the user must confirm in their calendar app. Do not present inactive or unpublished feeds as ready to subscribe.

description.description: A short description of this calendar, not the conversation or user profile.

assignee.description: Optional event assignee explicitly named in the schedule; not the connected account identity, email address or a user profile.

description.description: Only event notes the user intends to publish with this calendar. Never send chat history, credentials, health records or unrelated personal context.

end_date.description: Inclusive last calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD. Keep a printed multi-day range as one event unless the user asks otherwise.

facet_actors.description: Source-grounded participants or organizers (people, teams or organizations), not an invented audience such as everyone at a school. Extract from the source in the host. Reuse available facet values or existing tags with consistent spelling and language; do not retag unchanged fields.

facet_topic.description: Source-grounded stable category, not the full event title. Extract from the source in the host. Reuse available facet values or existing tags with consistent spelling and language; do not retag unchanged fields.

facet_venue.description: Source-grounded venue name. Extract from the source in the host. Reuse available facet values or existing tags with consistent spelling and language; do not retag unchanged fields.

location.description: The event venue explicitly supplied in the schedule or requested correction, not the user’s current, home or device location. Do not request or infer user geolocation.

external_key.description: Source-stable, namespaced event identity, for example school-a:session-104. Do not derive it from a mutable title or date. A duplicate add does not update the event; use its event_id with update.

request_id.description: Generate an opaque key for this save and reuse it unchanged for retries, to prevent duplicate changes. Not a user identifier, chat/session ID, or telemetry. Do not include personal data.

name: create_feed
